target_customer: Developers and companies building AI agents that need to use websites (for example Cash App and Rye)
problem: Agents that must operate websites with no API need fast, stealthy, observable cloud browsers that keep sessions and logins.
business_model: Usage-based cloud browser infrastructure with an open source core

founders.name: Catherine Jue
previous_startups: Sway Finance (YC S16, outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page says she led Cash App's forward deployed engineering team and docs platform.

founders.name: Rafael Garcia
previous_startups: Clever (YC S12, acquired for $500M in 2021 per YC page)

technical_complexity.rationale: Unikernel based browsers with sub-150ms cold starts, stealth, proxies and CAPTCHA solving at scale are hard infrastructure engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Open source core and several rivals (Browserbase, Steel, Anchor, Hyperbrowser); speed and reliability are the edge and can be matched.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; competitor comparison pages list Kernel alongside Browserbase, Steel, Anchor and Hyperbrowser in 2026.

market_need_then: Browser and computer use agents grew in 2025, and the company reports use by Cash App and Rye and over 11,000 teams by September 2026.

branding.domain_note: Uses kernel.sh and onkernel.com, not kernel.com.

identity.logo: Brand assets and naming guidelines page offered
identity.visual_style: Name written in all caps as KERNEL; developer centric
identity.voice_and_tone: Informal engineer voice ('crazy fast'), emoji in the YC description

branding.brand_signature: 'Crazy fast' speed positioning and the KERNEL all caps wordmark
branding.community_and_virality: Open source project and developer docs; Accel and SiliconANGLE coverage of the raise.

brand_strength.rationale: Short technical name that fits the unikernel product, with published brand guidelines, but it is a generic term without a notable mascot or community ritual.

outcome_analysis: Kernel raised a combined seed and Series A of $22M led by Accel in October 2025, within months of the Summer 2025 batch. Repeat founders (a prior YC exit) and the rise of browser agents drove fast traction, with 11,000 plus teams reported by September 2026. Competition from Browserbase and others and an open core keep defensibility moderate.
notes: Round is described by Axios and Accel as seed and Series A combined; recorded as series_a since Accel calls it the Series A lead, seed portion not separated. VCBacked lists $16M, likely stale. Competitor list left empty: comparison pages found were from 2026 and undated for 2025. Education of founders not found.
